name: BTS6133D
title: PROFET smart high-side power switch, 10 mΩ, with proportional load current sense
summary: A single-channel high-side switch for 12 V and 24 V grounded loads: an N-channel vertical power MOSFET with its own charge pump, a current-controlled input and a sense output whose current follows the load current at a ratio of about 10 000. It limits short-circuit current and latches off on a hard short, shuts down on overtemperature and restarts, clamps inductive kickback at about 42 V and survives load dump. Under reverse battery and inverse current the MOSFET is turned on rather than leaving the body diode to conduct. AEC qualified, in the 5-pin DPAK PG-TO252-5-11.

pins.name: OUT
pins.function: Load output. Join it to pin 5 on the board: with one of the two left unconnected, on-state resistance goes up, peak current capability goes down and sense accuracy suffers.

pins.name: IN
pins.function: Control input, driven by current. Pulling it to ground (through the input switch) turns the output on.

pins.name: Vbb
pins.function: Positive supply; tied to the tab inside the package. The footprint carries no pad for it.

pins.name: Vbb
pins.function: Positive supply and heat path; the drain of the power MOSFET.

pins.name: IS
pins.function: Sense output. In normal operation it sources a current proportional to load current; under overload, overtemperature or short-circuit shutdown it sources a fixed fault current (see the truth table).

pins.name: OUT
pins.function: Load output, the same node as pin 1; both must be connected together externally.

circuits.title: Basic high-side connection with current sense
circuits.description: The switch sits between the supply and a load returned to load ground. A switch from IN to logic ground turns it on by drawing input current. The sense current from IS flows through RIS to logic ground, so the voltage VIS across RIS reads the load current.
notes: U1.OUT stands for pins 1 and 5 joined; U1.Vbb for pin 3 and the tab.

circuits.title: Overvoltage protection of the logic part
circuits.description: External parts that keep the control and sense lines safe when the supply rises past the 67 V internal zeners. RIN sits in series with IN. RIS loads IS to signal ground as usual; RV leads the sense voltage onward to a zener VZ,VIS that clamps it to signal ground. Without RV and VZ,VIS the voltage between IS and ground can go above 5 V once the overvoltage passes 67 V typ.
notes: Rbb = 100 Ω typ inside the device; VZ,IN = VZ,IS = 67 V typ.

circuits.title: Reverse battery protection (Reversave)
circuits.description: With the battery reversed, current flows from signal ground into IN and IS and turns the power MOSFET on, so the load current passes through the channel instead of the body diode. RIN in the input line and RIS on the sense pin set that current; the diode D across the NPN input switch carries the input share. RIN is needed when the reverse voltage exceeds 16 V; the two resistors together should pass about 80 mA.
notes: RIN follows 1/RIN + 1/RIS = 0.08 A / (|Vbb| - 12 V).

circuits.title: Inverse current operation (Inversave)
circuits.description: The output is held above the supply by an outside source, so load current flows back from OUT to Vbb. Switching the input on lets the channel carry that current at RON(inv) instead of the body diode. Current sense gives only IIS(LH) in this mode.

circuits.title: Supply disconnect with an energised inductive load, version a
circuits.description: When the supply is cut while an inductive load carries current, the load current needs a path that does not run through the switch. A diode D1 and a zener DZ1 in series, anode to anode, across the load give it one. With RIN = 0, VZL + VD must stay under 39 V; a higher clamp needs the IN and IS currents limited to 120 mA. A plain diode or a varistor can take the place of the pair.

circuits.title: Short circuit test circuit
circuits.description: The supply reaches Vbb through a 5 µH and 10 mΩ primary impedance. The output feeds a secondary inductance LSC and resistance RSC into a load ZL; closing switch SC shorts the far end of RSC to ground.

circuits.title: Inductive load switch-off energy
circuits.description: An inductive load, inductance L with series resistance RL, hangs from OUT. When the input opens, the output clamps at VON(CL) below Vbb and the device absorbs EAS: the energy drawn from the supply during demagnetisation plus the energy stored in L, less what RL dissipates.

operation.text: IN is a current input. The output turns on when IN is pulled to ground and current flows out of it; the input switch must be able to sink IIN(on), 2.2 mA max. Below 30 µA the device is off. A 67 V typ zener from Vbb to IN protects it (15 mA max), and the logic is fed from Vbb through the internal resistor Rbb, 100 Ω typ.

An internal charge pump drives the gate of the N-channel MOSFET. Below VbIN(u) (2.5 V typ) the device shuts down; the charge pump starts again once Vbb reaches Vbb(ucp), 4 V typ. With the input on, VOUT follows Vbb from that restart up to the overvoltage clamp, where VON is held at VON(CL).

IS sources IL / kILIS while VOUT - VIS stays above 5 V, and saturates at IIS,lim (6.0 mA typ) with VON below 1 V. RIS of 1 kΩ is the nominal value, or 1 kΩ/n when n devices share one resistor. With a large RIS, VIS can climb almost to Vbb. The reading is not valid during the settling times after turn-on, turn-off and a change of load current. IS may be left open when sense is not used. The lowest load current that can be told from zero is IIS(LH) × kILIS. While VbIS stays below VZ,IS, the sense current does not exceed IIS,fault or IIS,lim, also during the inrush of motors and lamps.

With the input on, overload (VON between about 1 V and 3.5 V), short circuit and overtemperature each drive IS to the fixed current IIS,fault, 5.2 mA typ. In overload the output stays on; in short circuit and overtemperature it is off. With the input off, IS carries only the leakage IIS(LL). The fault signal appears tdelay(fault) after the input goes on.

The output current is limited, the limit falling in steps as VON rises. If VON is still above VON(SC), 3.5 V typ, after td(SC1) (650 µs typ) from turn-on, the device turns off and stays off until the input is released (IIN = 0); that is short-circuit type one. A short that arrives while the output is already on trips it within td(SC2), about 2 µs (type two). Full protection holds up to Vbb = 30 V, for secondary resistance RSC and inductance LSC no worse than the allowable combinations for each supply voltage.

At Tjt (175 °C typ, 150 °C min) the output turns off. It restarts on its own once Tj has fallen back below Tjt (hysteresis ΔTjt, 10 K typ) while the input is still on, and IS carries IIS,fault while it is off.

At switch-off of an inductive load the output is driven negative and clamped where VON reaches VON(CL), 42 V typ, which demagnetises the load quickly. The device absorbs the energy EAS; the largest load inductance for a single switch-off falls with load current, from about 1 H at 1.2 A to 22 µH at 100 A (Tj,start = 150 °C, Vbb = 12 V). The same clamp acts when the supply rises past the clamp voltage. IN and IS each have a 67 V typ zener to Vbb; above that an IS-to-ground voltage over 5 V is possible unless RV and VZ,VIS are fitted.

With the battery reversed the power MOSFET is turned on through IN and IS, so the load current runs in the channel at RON(rev). Up to 16 V of reverse voltage RIS alone suffices; above that RIN is added. Dissipation is lowest when about 80 mA in total flows into IN and IS, supplied through a small-signal diode across the input switch, a MOSFET as input switch, or a suitable RIS. The current through Rbb heats the chip and belongs in the thermal budget.

The device tolerates VOUT above Vbb with Vbb positive. With the input off only the body diode conducts and dissipation is high; with the input on, the channel conducts and the loss falls to RON(inv) × IL² within -IL(inv). Current sense reads IIS(LH) in this mode and there is no overtemperature protection.

operation.topic: Loss of supply with an inductive load
operation.text: If Vbb is disconnected while an inductive load carries current, an external path for that current is needed: a diode, a zener or a varistor across the load. With RIN = 0 the clamp VZL + VD stays below 39 V; for a higher clamp the currents into IN and IS are limited to 120 mA.
Several devices may be paralleled for more load current; with n devices in parallel RIS becomes 1 kΩ/n. Pins 1 and 5 are both the output and are joined on the board; pin 3 and the tab are both Vbb.
Listed protections also include loss of ground, loss of Vbb (with an external diode when the load is inductive), load dump and ESD. Standby current with the input open is 3 µA typ.
